transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Honestly, what made me make the appointment is... well, I feel like the warm part of me just shut off. Like, after work, I'll sit on the couch with my husband or try to watch my normal shows. I know I should feel some comfort, or even just a little happy to be relaxing, but... there’s just nothing there. I don't feel any of that right now.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you felt unusually elevated or energized compared with your usual self?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal days where I feel good or have enough energy to get through my shift, but I've never had a time where I felt unusually energized or anything like that. Just regular energy.
How long have you felt this way?
It's been about three weeks now. It started right after an accident at my job... a heavy pallet collapsed and injured one of my coworkers. Ever since that happened, I've just felt this way.
Since the accident, have you had unwanted memories or nightmares about what happened?

Yeah, I do. Out of nowhere, I’ll just... see that pallet coming down again. Or I'll hear the crash in my head. It happens a lot if a forklift beeps or somebody drops something in the warehouse. Whenever that happens, my stomach just turns.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding things that remind you of what happened, such as the warehouse, forklifts, or talking about the accident?

No, not really. I mean, I still go into the warehouse for my shifts every day. I can't exactly avoid it since it's my job. I still work around the forklifts and everything... I haven't been staying away from them or anything like that, even if the noises bother me. So, no, I haven't been avoiding things.
Since the accident, have you felt unusually on guard or easily startled?

Yeah, definitely. When I’m anywhere near receiving now, I just... I keep checking the racks and the pallet heights. I'm constantly looking at where the exits are and watching who’s moving behind me. It's like I can’t trust the floor to be safe for even a minute.
Since the accident, have you felt detached from yourself or as if things around you were unreal?

No, I don't think so. Um, everything feels pretty normal in that way. I mean, I'm definitely on edge like I said, but I don't feel detached from myself or like things are fake or anything like that. It all feels very real to me, honestly.
Since the accident, have you had trouble sleeping?

Yeah, I have. Most nights I just lie there... I'm completely exhausted after the late shift, but every time I start to drift off, I just jerk awake. I keep thinking I hear the pallets shifting. And honestly, if I do manage to sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really rested anyway.
Since the accident, have you had trouble concentrating on tasks?

No, not really. I mean, I can still focus on pulling my orders and getting my work done. I guess I get a little distracted when I'm checking the racks, like I mentioned before, but my actual concentration on the tasks themselves seems fine. I haven't noticed any real trouble with that.
Since the accident, have you been more irritable or prone to angry outbursts than you were before?

Yeah, I definitely have. I've been snapping at people over really small stuff lately. Like, just the other day, one of the seasonal guys set some boxes a little crooked, and I just... I heard myself getting sharp and loud with him before I could even pull it back. I just get frustrated so fast right now over things that wouldn't normally bother me.
Since the accident, have you been unusually jumpy or startled by sudden noises or unexpected movements?
No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, loud noises in the warehouse don't really bother me any more than they usually would. I haven't noticed myself jumping at things or anything like that.
